## Back-to-Back Duathlon Weekends

One week after Guelph, it was time to race again in Welland.

Coming into this event, the main question was simple: after Guelph, could I
still perform and still be competitive? Racing hard on consecutive weekends is
always a good way to find out what is really there and what is still missing.

Guelph had already taken a fair bit out of me. It was hilly, hard, and
important from a qualification point of view. Welland looked flatter and more
straightforward on paper, but that did not automatically mean easier. On a
flatter course there is less hiding. If the legs are not there, it shows.

---

## The Qualification Picture

Like Guelph, this race mattered for age-group qualification.

The goal is still the same: win the age group, or at least finish close enough
to give myself a realistic chance of qualifying for the World Championships.
That is what gives these races a different feel. It is not just about placing
well on the day. It is also about who is in the actual five-year age-group
qualification category, who has submitted an expression of interest, and who
will still matter once Triathlon Canada starts allocating spots.

That uncertainty is part of the game. You can race well, finish on the podium,
and still walk away not really knowing what it means yet.

---

## Race Morning

![](https://storage.googleapis.com/blogs_josa/sport/blog_assets/2026-06-28_WELLAND_SPRINT_DUATHLON/img/thumbnail/260628_Welland_01-0024.jpg)

I arrived early, got set up without any rush, and had time to look around and
see a few familiar faces. What I did not see much of were calves marked
`40-49`, which did not make the qualification picture any easier to read.

The morning was calm for me, but transition itself had a bit of chaos. One
athlete, clearly at their first race, turned up with a mountain bike and
seemed entirely unconcerned by the fact that they were not even racking it
properly, just leaning it against other athletes' racked bikes. That led to a
fair amount of discussion with the referees before things were sorted out.

Small details like that do not decide the race, but they definitely shape the
feel of the morning.

---

## A Different Kind of Course

The format here was `5/20/2.5`, which is the standard way to organise a sprint
duathlon. Even so, it is still strange how every race seems to do this a bit
differently. In Guelph the format was `2/20/5`, which changes the race quite a
lot, and not just because of the missing 500 metres. A long first run and a
short second run reward a very different type of pacing and a different type
of patience.

On paper, Welland looked like a course that should suit me better: flatter,
more honest, and more about sustained effort than repeated changes of rhythm.
That can be good news, but it also means you have to be ready to do the work.
There is less terrain to save you.


---

## Run 1

![](https://storage.googleapis.com/blogs_josa/sport/blog_assets/2026-06-28_WELLAND_SPRINT_DUATHLON/img/thumbnail/260628_Welland_02-0253.jpg)

I started the first run trying to stay under control. That part went
reasonably well, but even so I faded quite a bit toward the end. That was when
I saw two athletes with `40-49` on their calves come past me.

I was still close enough to them that the race did not feel gone, but it was
clear I was in for a fight if I wanted to finish at least third. That was also
assuming there was not someone else in the category even further ahead that I
had simply not seen.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

activities_metadata <- read.csv(
  "analysis_data/activities_metadata.csv",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

activities_data <- read.csv(
  "analysis_data/activities_data.csv",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  na.strings = c("NA", "")
)

run_1_id <- activities_metadata |>
  filter(EVENT_TYPE == "RUN") |>
  distinct(ID) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(ID)

run_1_data <- activities_data |>
  filter(ID == run_1_id) |>
  transmute(
    secs = as.numeric(SECS),
    distance_km = KM,
    altitude_m = ALT,
    pace_min_km = as.numeric(PACE),
    hr_bpm = na_if(as.numeric(HR), 0),
    power_w = na_if(as.numeric(WATTS), 0)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(pace_min_km))

pace_min <- min(run_1_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)
pace_max <- max(run_1_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)
hr_min <- min(run_1_data$hr_bpm, na.rm = TRUE)
hr_max <- max(run_1_data$hr_bpm, na.rm = TRUE)
power_min <- min(run_1_data$power_w, na.rm = TRUE)
power_max <- max(run_1_data$power_w, na.rm = TRUE)
alt_min <- min(run_1_data$altitude_m, na.rm = TRUE)
alt_max <- max(run_1_data$altitude_m, na.rm = TRUE)

alt_span <- alt_max - alt_min

if (pace_max == pace_min) {
  pace_max <- pace_min + 1
}

if (hr_max == hr_min) {
  hr_max <- hr_min + 1
}

if (power_max == power_min) {
  power_max <- power_min + 1
}

scale_altitude <- function(altitude, y_min, y_max) {
  y_min + ((altitude - alt_min) / ifelse(alt_span == 0, 1, alt_span)) *
    (y_max - y_min)
}

scale_power_to_hr <- function(power) {
  hr_min + ((power - power_min) / (power_max - power_min)) * (hr_max - hr_min)
}

scale_hr_to_power <- function(hr) {
  power_min + ((hr - hr_min) / (hr_max - hr_min)) * (power_max - power_min)
}

run_1_plot_data <- run_1_data |>
  mutate(
    altitude_scaled_hr = scale_altitude(altitude_m, hr_min, hr_max),
    power_scaled_hr = scale_power_to_hr(power_w)
  )

pace_plot_start_secs <- run_1_plot_data |>
  filter(pace_min_km <= 4) |>
  summarise(start_secs = min(secs, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(start_secs)

run_1_pace_plot_data <- run_1_plot_data |>
  filter(secs >= pace_plot_start_secs)

pace_plot_min <- min(run_1_pace_plot_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)
pace_plot_max <- max(run_1_pace_plot_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)

if (pace_plot_max == pace_plot_min) {
  pace_plot_max <- pace_plot_min + 1
}

run_1_pace_plot_data <- run_1_pace_plot_data |>
  mutate(
    altitude_scaled_pace = scale_altitude(altitude_m, pace_plot_min, pace_plot_max)
  )

ggplot(run_1_plot_data, aes(x = distance_km)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = hr_min, ymax = altitude_scaled_hr),
    fill = "grey55",
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = hr_bpm),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "red",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = power_scaled_hr),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "#1f4e79",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "HR [bpm]",
    limits = c(hr_min, hr_max),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ scale_hr_to_power(.), name = "Power [W]")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Distance [km]",
    title = "Run 1 altitude, heart rate, and power over distance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

```

---

## Bike

As always, I struggled a bit getting the left shoe on after the mount line.
Not as badly as in Guelph, but still not clean. That was exactly when one of
the two `40-49` athletes who had passed me on the run came past me again on
the bike. So I had actually done the transition better overall, but the messy
mount still cost me the position again.

That only lasted about 500 metres. At the first turnaround he was right in
front of me and had to stop with a puncture. Brutally unlucky. I would have
been furious. We will never know whether I would have beaten him fairly in the
race, but on this day that was the end of his race.

After that I settled in on the bike and rode within myself. This is clearly my
strongest discipline at the moment. A few riders passed me, but none were in
my age group. Most of them were on fancy TT bikes as well, which does make me
want one.

At around kilometre 3, the other `40-49` athlete who had passed me earlier on
the run came by as well. He was putting in a strong ride. I stayed with him
until around kilometre 5, where there was a rise. I attacked there, and that
was enough to break him. By the end of the bike I had put roughly two minutes
into him.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

bike_id <- activities_metadata |>
  filter(EVENT_TYPE == "BIKE") |>
  distinct(ID) |>
  slice(1) |>
  pull(ID)

rolling_time_avg <- function(values, secs, window_seconds = 10) {
  vapply(seq_along(values), function(i) {
    in_window <- secs >= (secs[i] - window_seconds) & secs <= secs[i]
    mean(values[in_window], na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))
}

bike_data <- activities_data |>
  filter(ID == bike_id) |>
  transmute(
    secs = as.numeric(SECS),
    distance_km = KM,
    altitude_m = ALT,
    power_w = na_if(as.numeric(WATTS), 0),
    hr_bpm = na_if(as.numeric(HR), 0)
  ) |>
  arrange(secs) |>
  mutate(
    power_10s_w = rolling_time_avg(power_w, secs),
    hr_10s_bpm = rolling_time_avg(hr_bpm, secs)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(power_10s_w))

power_min <- min(bike_data$power_10s_w, na.rm = TRUE)
power_max <- max(bike_data$power_10s_w, na.rm = TRUE)
hr_min <- min(bike_data$hr_10s_bpm, na.rm = TRUE)
hr_max <- max(bike_data$hr_10s_bpm, na.rm = TRUE)
alt_min <- min(bike_data$altitude_m, na.rm = TRUE)
alt_max <- max(bike_data$altitude_m, na.rm = TRUE)

hr_plot_min <- 140
hr_plot_max <- hr_max
alt_span <- alt_max - alt_min

if (power_max == power_min) {
  power_max <- power_min + 1
}

if (hr_plot_max == hr_plot_min) {
  hr_plot_max <- hr_plot_min + 1
}

scale_altitude <- function(altitude, y_min, y_max) {
  y_min + ((altitude - alt_min) / ifelse(alt_span == 0, 1, alt_span)) *
    (y_max - y_min)
}

scale_power_to_hr <- function(power) {
  hr_plot_min + ((power - power_min) / (power_max - power_min)) *
    (hr_plot_max - hr_plot_min)
}

scale_hr_to_power <- function(hr) {
  power_min + ((hr - hr_plot_min) / (hr_plot_max - hr_plot_min)) *
    (power_max - power_min)
}

bike_plot_data <- bike_data |>
  mutate(
    altitude_scaled_hr = scale_altitude(altitude_m, hr_plot_min, hr_plot_max),
    power_scaled_hr = scale_power_to_hr(power_10s_w)
  )

ggplot(bike_plot_data, aes(x = distance_km)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = hr_plot_min, ymax = altitude_scaled_hr),
    fill = "grey55",
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = hr_10s_bpm),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "red",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = power_scaled_hr),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "#1f4e79",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "HR [bpm]",
    limits = c(hr_plot_min, hr_plot_max),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ scale_hr_to_power(.), name = "Power [W]")
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Distance [km]",
    title = "Bike altitude, heart rate, and power over distance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Run 2

![](https://storage.googleapis.com/blogs_josa/sport/blog_assets/2026-06-28_WELLAND_SPRINT_DUATHLON/img/thumbnail/260628_Welland_FinishLine-0052.jpg)

My main focus on the second run was simply to stay strong enough not to get
passed again. I knew the guy I had dropped on the bike was probably a bit
faster than me on the run, but I did not know exactly how far ahead I was or
whether it was enough to hold him off.

This was not a fun run. I started to struggle, with fatigue and maybe also the
heat, and the pace dropped badly. At the same time I could not see anyone with
`40-49` on their calves ahead of me, so I never had the visual target that
might have helped me push harder. I was hoping I was racing for first, but in
practice I was running defensively, trying at the very least not to let anyone
come back to me.

About 20 metres from the finish line I heard someone sprinting behind me.
Not knowing who it was, I had no choice but to sprint as well in case it was
the athlete from my category finally catching me. I managed to hold him off,
only to find out afterwards that he was in the `20-29` category, so it would
not have changed anything in my own race.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

run_2_id <- activities_metadata |>
  filter(EVENT_TYPE == "RUN") |>
  distinct(ID) |>
  slice(2) |>
  pull(ID)

run_2_data <- activities_data |>
  filter(ID == run_2_id) |>
  transmute(
    secs = as.numeric(SECS),
    distance_km = KM,
    altitude_m = ALT,
    pace_min_km = as.numeric(PACE),
    hr_bpm = na_if(as.numeric(HR), 0),
    power_w = na_if(as.numeric(WATTS), 0)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(pace_min_km))

pace_min <- min(run_2_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)
pace_max <- max(run_2_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)
hr_min <- min(run_2_data$hr_bpm, na.rm = TRUE)
hr_max <- max(run_2_data$hr_bpm, na.rm = TRUE)
has_run_2_power <- any(!is.na(run_2_data$power_w))
power_min <- if (has_run_2_power) min(run_2_data$power_w, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
power_max <- if (has_run_2_power) max(run_2_data$power_w, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_
alt_min <- min(run_2_data$altitude_m, na.rm = TRUE)
alt_max <- max(run_2_data$altitude_m, na.rm = TRUE)

alt_span <- alt_max - alt_min

if (pace_max == pace_min) {
  pace_max <- pace_min + 1
}

if (hr_max == hr_min) {
  hr_max <- hr_min + 1
}

if (has_run_2_power && power_max == power_min) {
  power_max <- power_min + 1
}

scale_altitude <- function(altitude, y_min, y_max) {
  y_min + ((altitude - alt_min) / ifelse(alt_span == 0, 1, alt_span)) *
    (y_max - y_min)
}

run_2_plot_data <- run_2_data |>
  mutate(
    altitude_scaled_hr = scale_altitude(altitude_m, hr_min, hr_max)
  )

if (has_run_2_power) {
  scale_power_to_hr <- function(power) {
    hr_min + ((power - power_min) / (power_max - power_min)) * (hr_max - hr_min)
  }

  scale_hr_to_power <- function(hr) {
    power_min + ((hr - hr_min) / (hr_max - hr_min)) * (power_max - power_min)
  }

  run_2_plot_data <- run_2_plot_data |>
    mutate(
      power_scaled_hr = scale_power_to_hr(power_w)
    )
}

run_2_pace_plot_data <- run_2_plot_data

pace_plot_min <- min(run_2_pace_plot_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)
pace_plot_max <- max(run_2_pace_plot_data$pace_min_km, na.rm = TRUE)

if (pace_plot_max == pace_plot_min) {
  pace_plot_max <- pace_plot_min + 1
}

run_2_pace_plot_data <- run_2_pace_plot_data |>
  mutate(
    altitude_scaled_pace = scale_altitude(altitude_m, pace_plot_min, pace_plot_max)
  )

run_2_hr_power_plot <- ggplot(run_2_plot_data, aes(x = distance_km)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = hr_min, ymax = altitude_scaled_hr),
    fill = "grey55",
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = hr_bpm),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "red",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Distance [km]",
    title = if (has_run_2_power) {
      "Run 2 altitude, heart rate, and power over distance"
    } else {
      "Run 2 altitude and heart rate over distance"
    }
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)

if (has_run_2_power) {
  run_2_hr_power_plot <- run_2_hr_power_plot +
    geom_line(
      aes(y = power_scaled_hr),
      linewidth = 0.7,
      color = "#1f4e79",
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "HR [bpm]",
      limits = c(hr_min, hr_max),
      sec.axis = sec_axis(~ scale_hr_to_power(.), name = "Power [W]")
    )
} else {
  run_2_hr_power_plot <- run_2_hr_power_plot +
    scale_y_continuous(
      name = "HR [bpm]",
      limits = c(hr_min, hr_max)
    )
}

run_2_hr_power_plot

ggplot(run_2_pace_plot_data, aes(x = distance_km)) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(ymin = pace_plot_min, ymax = altitude_scaled_pace),
    fill = "grey55",
    alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = pace_min_km),
    linewidth = 0.7,
    color = "#1f4e79"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Pace [min/km]",
    limits = c(pace_plot_min, pace_plot_max)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Distance [km]",
    title = "Run 2 altitude and pace over distance"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11)
```

## Result and What It Means

The final result was third in category. That is a podium, which is never a bad
thing, but I was still a bit disappointed. Realistically, this was not the
best possible outcome for qualification chances. At the same time, it was a
fair defeat. The two athletes ahead of me were simply too strong on the day.

What happens next depends on details that are still outside my control: 
the exact age of everyone next year and who submitted their EOI. As usual,
 we now wait for the federation to do its homework and tell everyone where 
 things actually stand.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

format_finish_time <- function(seconds) {
  total_seconds <- round(as.numeric(seconds))
  hours <- total_seconds %/% 3600
  minutes <- (total_seconds %% 3600) %/% 60
  secs <- total_seconds %% 60
  sprintf("%d:%02d:%02d", hours, minutes, secs)
}

all_races <- read.csv(
  "analysis_data/all_races.csv",
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

top_men_40_49 <- all_races |>
  filter(CATEGORY == "Men40-49") |>
  arrange(RANKING_CATEGORY) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |>
  transmute(
    Name = ATHLETE,
    `Age Group Rank` = RANKING_CATEGORY,
    `Overall Rank` = RANKING_OVERALL,
    `Finishing Time` = format_finish_time(RESULT_FINAL)
  )

knitr::kable(top_men_40_49, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

---

## Final Thoughts

Overall, mixed feelings. Third place is still a podium finish, and backing up
Guelph with another competitive race one week later is not nothing. But it was
also obvious that my run is still lagging behind where it needs to be. There
is work to do there. I probably also need to lose a bit of weight. The bike is
another possible limiter, although that is not something I can really solve
immediately.

There is still one more proper chance to qualify cleanly: Barrie on August 9.
On paper that is another course that should suit me well because it is flat.
At the same time, it is also a competitive race, so there will be no easy way
through. Looking at last year's results, I could have won there, but last year
it was not a qualifying event. This year it is, which will likely make it a
very different race.

<div class="race-lightbox" id="race-lightbox" aria-hidden="true">
  <button class="race-lightbox__close" type="button" aria-label="Close gallery">&times;</button>
  <button class="race-lightbox__nav race-lightbox__nav--prev" type="button" aria-label="Previous image">&#8249;</button>
  <img class="race-lightbox__image" src="" alt="">
  <button class="race-lightbox__nav race-lightbox__nav--next" type="button" aria-label="Next image">&#8250;</button>
</div>

<script>
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  const gallery = document.getElementById("race-gallery");
  const lightbox = document.getElementById("race-lightbox");
  const image = lightbox.querySelector(".race-lightbox__image");
  const closeButton = lightbox.querySelector(".race-lightbox__close");
  const prevButton = lightbox.querySelector(".race-lightbox__nav--prev");
  const nextButton = lightbox.querySelector(".race-lightbox__nav--next");
  const thumbs = Array.from(gallery.querySelectorAll(".race-gallery__thumb"));
  let activeIndex = 0;

  function showImage(index) {
    activeIndex = (index + thumbs.length) % thumbs.length;
    const thumb = thumbs[activeIndex];
    const thumbImage = thumb.querySelector("img");
    image.src = thumb.dataset.full;
    image.alt = thumbImage.alt;
    lightbox.classList.add("is-open");
    lightbox.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "false");
    document.body.style.overflow = "hidden";
  }

  function closeLightbox() {
    lightbox.classList.remove("is-open");
    lightbox.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
    image.src = "";
    document.body.style.overflow = "";
  }

  thumbs.forEach(function (thumb, index) {
    thumb.addEventListener("click", function (event) {
      event.preventDefault();
      showImage(index);
    });
  });

  closeButton.addEventListener("click", closeLightbox);
  prevButton.addEventListener("click", function () { showImage(activeIndex - 1); });
  nextButton.addEventListener("click", function () { showImage(activeIndex + 1); });

  lightbox.addEventListener("click", function (event) {
    if (event.target === lightbox) {
      closeLightbox();
    }
  });

  document.addEventListener("keydown", function (event) {
    if (!lightbox.classList.contains("is-open")) {
      return;
    }
    if (event.key === "Escape") {
      closeLightbox();
    }
    if (event.key === "ArrowLeft") {
      showImage(activeIndex - 1);
    }
    if (event.key === "ArrowRight") {
      showImage(activeIndex + 1);
    }
  });
});
</script>
